FIXES APPLIED: (1 blocker) page order is the world's own: ascending page numbers 100, 101, 400, 500, 800, instead of the incumbent hero>features>price>faq order; and the FAQ is split by the page it answers (track-me and accounts filed on P400 beside the ledger, alternatives on P500; who-makes and how-money on P800, below the frame) - that is the grouping change, not just a reorder. In the static mobile frame the fixed Fastext bar sits over scrolled content and clips the top edge of the MONEY & BILLS band just below it.
selfVerdict: Reads unmistakably as its own world with the name covered: black ground, full-saturation teletext colours each with one job, a mosaic LAGERLAND on a blue band, double-height yellow Tiny5 H1, page numbers on every line, a four-colour Fastext row as the sticky bar, and the Xiangqiful coin art on air behind boxed lines (MIX) with the official badge, QR and verbatim price in the subtitle panel. Working parts are real (PAGE field, need index with squircle chips on mobile, ledger table, dot-leader Versus list), not a poster; the lower half proves it holds as a page, not just a hero, and the filed-FAQ grouping is distinct from the usual hero>features>FAQ order. Honest weaknesses: the first viewport can still be read as copy-left/picture-right even though the picture is a MIX backdrop behind boxed lines; the text slab hides the coin's left rim; the lower half is sparse and text-only (pure black with colour bands), so it relies on teletext nostalgia that US visitors may not share; Tiny5 at 16px (newsflash, table heads) is at the edge of comfortable on phones; the pixel star reads as a generic sparkle rather than the stone mark. Verdict: strongest on memorability and routing, weakest on warmth; would ship if the owner wants the studio to feel like a broadcaster, not a shop.
